name: native-toggle-repaints-every-surface
description:
SetOpaqueSurround only called PushSidebarAppearance, and neither it nor the crossfade completion in StepSurroundFade called PushAiPanelInk, so the command bar (and the rest of the nine-surface fan-out) kept ink computed against the previous surround after a LIVE Native app view toggle - only a surface's own one-shot ready handshake ever caught it up, which is why the defect hides at startup and this scenario toggles rather than launches into the new state. Fixed by adding PushAiPanelInk() to the end of SetOpaqueSurround and to StepSurroundFade's completion.

reads the command bar's surround tokens before the toggle and again after the crossfade finishes - opened ONCE before the toggle and never reopened, the same technique a sibling scenario's scenario uses for the same reason, so CommandBarWidget::Show's own re-push on open cannot be mistaken for the live fan-out. The fixture (ambilight.spaces.json + a page carrying its own tint) guarantees has_backdrop_tint_ is true, so the toggle actually takes the crossfade branch rather than snapping - the crossfade's completion must push too, not only the toggle's start.
The deciding assertion: eval_changed on the command bar's tokens.

Also reads the settings window across the same toggle. Settings is always native, so it must stay native on both sides of the toggle.

actions.note: the window paints its tint, which is what the fade needs to fade from
open the command bar ONCE, before the toggle - CommandBarWidget::Show re-pushes the theme on every open

actions.expression: (() => { const r = document.documentElement; const s = getComputedStyle(r); const t = (n) => (s.getPropertyValue(n) || '').trim().toLowerCase(); return 'surround=' + t('--atrium-surround-color') + ' ink=' + t('--atrium-surround-ink') + ' native=' + r.classList.contains('atrium-native-chrome'); })()
actions.note: read before the toggle - opaqueSurround starts false in the staged settings

actions.note: round-trip margin after the fade's own completion push

actions.expression: (() => { const r = document.documentElement; const s = getComputedStyle(r); const t = (n) => (s.getPropertyValue(n) || '').trim().toLowerCase(); return 'surround=' + t('--atrium-surround-color') + ' ink=' + t('--atrium-surround-ink') + ' native=' + r.classList.contains('atrium-native-chrome'); })()
actions.note: THE DECIDING READ: never reopened, so this can only be the live fan-out from SetOpaqueSurround/StepSurroundFade
